title: The Landfall of Mount Kessler
premise: Silas Pemberton, a desert ranger who has spent years outrunning her past, is hired by old rival Maren Kessler to escort a survey crew up the Kessler River to its forbidden source before monsoon season seals the highlands. The job was sworn off after an expedition years ago that killed Silas's mentor and scattered the crew she once called family — and Maren knows it, because she caused it. As the river narrows and the truth of that disaster surfaces, Silas discovers Maren seeks not water but the source's mineral claim, and she must choose between loyalty to the found family reassembling around her and the truth that could destroy them all. When the monsoon makes landfall, Silas breaks the dam of silence at the source itself, exposing Maren's corruption and leading her ragged crew back downriver — not as survivors of the past, but as a family that finally chose each other over its secrets.
about_author: Freya Joubert is a former river guide who spent six seasons in the Karoo before turning to fiction full-time. She writes adventure novels about landscapes that remember what people try to forget.

chapters.title: Nothing to Cross
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Tracking a horse thief across the empty flats, Silas reflects on why she never stops moving: stillness invites memory. She catches the thief but lets him go for reasons she won't name. Emotional beat: loneliness worn like armor, establishing the cost of stopping.

chapters.title: The Rival's Letter
chapters.summary: POV Silas. A courier delivers Maren Kessler's offer: lead a survey crew up the Kessler River, triple pay, before monsoon. The name alone is a wound — the river, the expedition, the mentor she lost. Silas burns the letter, then digs it out of the ash. Beat: temptation wrapped in grief.

chapters.title: Crew of Ghosts
chapters.summary: POV Silas. In the border town of Vell's Landing, Silas finds the old crew half-reassembled: engineer Odile, navigator Tam, and a stranger named Bo who claims to be her dead mentor's nephew. Old grudges flare; Odile refuses until Silas admits she needs them. Beat: reluctant reunion, family forming against will.

chapters.title: Terms of Silence
chapters.summary: POV Maren. Maren meets the crew privately, imposing one condition: no talk of the first expedition. Her POV reveals she's hiding more than grief — there are documents aboard her barge she cannot let anyone read. Beat: charm as control; the reader sees her corruption early.

chapters.title: Upstream
chapters.summary: POV Silas. The barge enters the gorge country. Rapids test the crew; Bo saves Tam from drowning and earns his place. At night Silas catches Maren burning papers and says nothing. Beat: competence and camaraderie building, unease underneath.

chapters.title: The Drowned Camp
chapters.summary: POV Odile. They pass the ruins of the first expedition's camp, flooded by a weir no map records. Odile recognizes the engineering — someone built it to hide something upstream. Silas realizes the river was rewritten. Beat: the past made physical; suspicion hardens.

chapters.title: What Tam Read
chapters.summary: POV Tam. Tam salvages a waterlogged logbook from the drowned camp bearing his own handwriting from years ago — pages he doesn't remember writing, or chose to forget. He hides it from Silas. Beat: guilt as private burden; loyalty beginning to strain against truth.

chapters.title: Portage of Bones
chapters.summary: POV Silas. A grueling portage around the weir uncovers remains — the expedition's missing guide. Maren claims bandits; Bo quietly tells Silas the guide died protecting the source's location. First open fracture between Silas and Maren. Beat: grief weaponized into resolve.

chapters.title: The Monsoon Bell
chapters.summary: POV Maren. Word arrives: the monsoon is early. Maren pushes the crew harder, offering bonuses, revealing her desperation. Privately she orders her hired muscle, Dray, to watch Silas. Beat: ticking clock set; power tightening its grip.

chapters.title: River Country
chapters.summary: POV Bo. Bo shares his uncle's letters with Silas around the fire — evidence the first expedition found ore veins worth kingdoms, and that Maren sabotaged their retreat to keep the claim secret. Silas confronts what following Maren means. Beat: truth arriving as gift from new family.

chapters.title: The Turn at Kettle Falls
chapters.summary: POV Silas. At Kettle Falls the barge must be abandoned; the crew goes on foot. Odile wants to turn back; Tam, reading his recovered logbook aloud, admits he helped falsify the first expedition's report under Maren's orders. The crew fractures. Beat: confession as crisis.

chapters.title: Split Water
chapters.summary: POV Tam. Tam tries to make amends by stealing Maren's remaining documents; Dray catches him. Tam escapes wounded and warns the camp: Maren intends to reach the source first and seal it behind her with dynamite. Beat: betrayal answered with sacrifice; stakes made lethal.

chapters.title: Storm Signs
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Weather turning, Odile calculates they have three days. She proposes racing Maren's party up the canyon rather than retreating — using the flood itself to trap Maren's claim forever. Silas must decide whether to fight or flee. Beat: courage chosen over survival instinct.

chapters.title: The Ascent
chapters.summary: POV Silas. The climb through slot canyons as rain begins. Dray ambushes them; Bo takes a fall saving Silas and is left in Odile's care while Silas presses on with Tam. Beat: cost counted in bodies; determination sharpened by loss.

chapters.title: Source of the Kessler
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Silas reaches the source: a spring-fed cavern laced with raw ore, beautiful and damning. Maren waits with the dynamite already placed, and offers Silas partnership — wealth, absolution, an end to running. Beat: temptation at its purest; the theme crystallized.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Price
chapters.summary: POV Maren. Maren's POV lays bare her logic: the world rewarded her ruthlessness every time, and punished honesty with graves. She lights the fuse. Silas chooses truth — tackling Maren into the water as the charge blows the cavern mouth. Beat: climax; choice made physical.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: POV Silas. The monsoon hits in full as the source floods. Silas drags a broken Maren to high ground; Tam and Odile arrive with ropes. The ore claim drowns beneath the rising river — unownable now, free forever. Beat: catharsis; nature rendering judgment.

chapters.title: Downriver
chapters.summary: POV Odile. The descent, hauling Maren as prisoner. Maren, delirious, confesses everything to the river. Odile keeps the crew alive through the flood with the skill of someone who has finally forgiven herself for the first expedition. Beat: exhaustion transfigured into grace.

chapters.title: The Testimony
chapters.summary: POV Tam. At Vell's Landing, Tam surrenders the forged report to the magistrate, accepting his share of blame. His honesty shields the others and buries Maren's claim legally as well as physically. Beat: truth repaying loyalty at last.

chapters.title: What Stopping Costs
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Maren is taken away without apology; Silas feels not triumph but emptiness — vengeance closes nothing. Bo asks what she'll do now. For the first time, Silas doesn't answer by leaving. Beat: the wound examined; armor loosening.

chapters.title: A House Above the Weir
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Spring. The crew rebuilds the drowned camp as a waystation for travelers on the river — a home instead of a grave. Odile engineers, Tam maps, Bo guides, Silas stays. Beat: found family made literal in timber and stone.

chapters.title: The River Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Silas, closing frame. A stranger arrives asking about the forbidden source; Silas tells him only the true parts. Watching the water run clean past the old weir, she understands the river kept what mattered and gave back the rest. Beat: resolution — stillness finally chosen, and survivable.
